title: Opentrons OT-2 Workflow for Cayman His-tag Detection ELISA Kit
author: Ben Braverman
materials: Prepare all kit reagents according to the Cayman His-Tag Detection ELISA Kit manual before loading the OT-2 deck.

steps.title: Pre‑chill aluminum blocks
steps.instruction: Place the Opentrons 24‑well aluminum block and the 96‑well aluminum block adapter in a –20 °C freezer for at least 2 h before starting.

steps.title: Open plate‑map generator
steps.instruction: Open the ELISA plate‑map generator HTML file from the GitHub repository in a web browser; no installation or dependencies are required.

steps.title: Auto‑fill sample layout
steps.instruction: In the “Auto‑Fill Samples” panel set the number of replicates (e.g., 2), enter the total number of samples, choose Horizontal or Vertical orientation, then click “Fill Samples” to assign sequential well numbers (A1 = sample 1, A2 = sample 2, …).

steps.title: Assign standards and controls
steps.instruction: Select wells on the grid, open the “Assign Content” panel and assign: S1–S6 standards (enter standard number 1‑6, corresponding to the 3 µg/mL‑0.093 µg/mL dilution series, typically in duplicate), B0 maximum‑binding control (TBS + tracer + antibody, duplicate), NSB non‑specific‑binding control (TBS + tracer only, duplicate), and Blk blank (no reagents during loading, duplicate). You may also type directly into selected wells.

steps.title: Add optional sample IDs
steps.instruction: In the “Sample Key” panel paste a list of descriptive IDs (one per line) and click “Apply Bulk IDs”; the IDs are saved in the CSV but not used by the OT‑2 scripts.

steps.title: Download and upload CSV
steps.instruction: Click “Download CSV”, then in the Opentrons app (step #3) upload this file via the “Plate Layout CSV” parameter.

steps.title: Prepare TBS assay buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute the 10× TBS concentrate with 90 mL UltraPure water (final volume ≈ 100 mL). Aliquot at least 1 000 µL of the resulting TBS assay buffer into a 1.5 mL snap‑cap tube.

steps.title: Prepare standard dilution series
steps.instruction: Serially dilute standards S1–S6 in TBS assay buffer according to the kit manual, then load each standard into a 1.5 mL snap‑cap tube containing at least 1 000 µL.

steps.title: Prepare His‑AP tracer solution
steps.instruction: Resuspend the His‑AP tracer vial with 6 mL TBS assay buffer. Aliquot 1 300 µL of this solution into each required 1.5 mL tube (provides 1 000 µL usable volume with 300 µL dead volume). Plan roughly one tube per 20 wells that will receive tracer (all wells except Blk) and do not exceed 1 300 µL per tube.

steps.title: Prepare His ELISA antibody solution
steps.instruction: Resuspend the His ELISA monoclonal antibody vial with 6 mL TBS assay buffer. Aliquot 1 300 µL into each required 1.5 mL tube, planning about one tube per 20 wells that will receive antibody (all wells except NSB and Blk).

steps.title: Load samples into PCR plate
steps.instruction: Dispense each sample into the Bio‑Rad 96‑well PCR plate in row‑major order matching the plate‑map numbers (sample 1 → A1, sample 2 → A2, …). Add 50 µL per replicate; keep total volume per well ≤ 125 µL to avoid overflow.

steps.title: Set up OT‑2 deck for loading
steps.instruction: Place all labware (ELISA strip plate, reagent tubes, tip racks, etc.) on the deck positions shown in the OT‑2 “Labware & Liquids” map. Ensure caps of 1.5 mL tubes face outward to avoid interference.

steps.title: Upload sample‑loading script
steps.instruction: In the Opentrons app import ot2_p1000single_elisa_sample_filling_final.py, upload the CSV plate map, set “Test Mode” to true for a dry run or false for the actual experiment, and verify that tip‑rack count and reagent volumes match your preparations.

steps.title: Run sample‑loading script
steps.instruction: Execute the script; it performs five transfer blocks using a new P1000 tip for each transfer: (1) TBS → NSB wells (100 µL) and B0 wells (50 µL); (2) Standards S1‑S6 → assigned wells (50 µL each); (3) Samples → assigned wells (50 µL each); (4) His‑AP tracer → all occupied wells except Blk (50 µL each); (5) Antibody → all occupied wells except NSB and Blk (50 µL each). All dispense 1 mm above the well bottom at 20 % of the default pipette speed.

steps.title: Incubate after loading
steps.instruction: Remove the ELISA strip plate, seal with adhesive film, place on an orbital shaker and incubate 90 min at room temperature with gentle agitation. For high‑sample runs that would overflow the default tip trash, use the waste‑chute variant (ot2_p1000single_elisa_sample_filling_waste_chute.py) which drops tips into a 3D‑printed chute at slot 10; first validate positioning with tests/ot2_tip_drop_waste_chute_test.py.

steps.title: Prepare AP wash buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute the AP wash buffer concentrate 1:150 with UltraPure water. Prepare 11 mL of this buffer for each plate column that will be used (e.g., 5 columns → 55 mL). Prepare extra to cover dead volume; store at 4 °C if made in advance.

steps.title: Prepare pNPP substrate
steps.instruction: Thaw the pNPP substrate on ice, keep at 4 °C until use, and plan for ~2 mL per column being washed. The wash/substrate script includes a pause after the wash cycles so you can load the substrate at that point, minimizing light and temperature exposure.

steps.title: Set up OT‑2 deck for wash/substrate
steps.instruction: Arrange labware for the wash and substrate protocol according to the OT‑2 “Labware & Liquids” map (including the ELISA strip plate, NEST 12‑channel reservoirs for wash buffer and substrate, tip racks, and waste reservoir).

steps.title: Upload wash/substrate script
steps.instruction: Import ot2_p300multi_elisa_wash_substrate.py into the Opentrons app, set “Number of Columns” to the number of columns used in your plate map (1‑12), and choose “Test Mode” as desired.

steps.title: Fill wash buffer reservoir
steps.instruction: In slot 4, fill the NEST 12‑channel reservoir with 11 mL of prepared AP wash buffer per channel, one channel for each plate column used (e.g., columns 1‑5 receive 11 mL each).

steps.title: Run wash and substrate script
steps.instruction: Execute the script (runs at 50 % default speed) which performs: (1) Supernatant removal – aspirate 195 µL from each column (0.8 mm above well bottom), dispense to waste, leave 5 µL airgap; use a fresh tip per column. (2) Six wash cycles – each cycle fill every column with 195 µL AP wash buffer (dispensed 3.5 mm below the well top) then aspirate 195 µL to waste; reuse the same tips across cycles. (3) Pause – load ~2 mL pNPP substrate into channels 1 and 2 of the NEST reservoir in slot 6, then resume. (4) Substrate addition – dispense 200 µL pNPP into each column from the well top using fresh tips; the script switches from channel 1 to channel 2 when the first is depleted. After completion, remove the plate, seal, and incubate ~60 min at room temperature protected from light.

steps.title: Read plate on spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance of the ELISA strip plate at 405–420 nm (recommended 415 nm) every 10 min for 90 min to capture the optimal colorimetric signal.
